terms: Imperfect subjunctive
A literary tense formed from the past historic stem, rarely used in modern speech.
Irregular subjunctive verbs
Verbs like etre, avoir, aller, faire, pouvoir, savoir, vouloir that have unique subjunctive stems.
Past subjunctive
Compound form using the subjunctive of avoir or etre plus the past participle.
Regular subjunctive endings
-e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent added to the stem of the third-person plural present indicative.
Subjunctive (le subjonctif)
A mood expressing doubt, necessity, emotion, or subjectivity, typically after que.
Trigger phrases
Expressions such as il faut que, bien que, avant que, pour que that require the subjunctive.

terms: La famille recomposée

Parenthood — covers shared roles of mothers and fathers; congé parental is parental leave.

Divorce — roughly 45% of French marriages end in divorce; consensual divorce was simplified in 2017.

Same-sex marriage legalised in France in 2013 under the Taubira law.
Reflexive verbs (pronominaux)
Verbs like se marier, s'entendre, se disputer that take être in the passé composé and agree with the subject.
La focalisation externe
External focalisation: only observable actions are described, like a camera.
La focalisation interne
Internal focalisation: events filtered through a character's consciousness.
La focalisation zero
Omniscient narrator with unlimited knowledge of all characters.
Le narrateur
The narrator: the voice telling the story, distinct from the author.
Le narrateur omniscient
An all-knowing narrator who sees everything, including characters' thoughts.
Le point de vue
Point of view: the perspective from which events are presented.
L'immigration asiatique
Migration from former Indochina (Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos), particularly post-1975.
L'immigration maghrebine
Migration from Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia, especially after WWII and decolonisation.
L'immigration subsaharienne
Migration from sub-Saharan African countries, growing since the 1970s.
La deuxieme generation
Second generation: children of immigrants born in France.
Le regroupement familial
Family reunification, formally allowed from 1976 after 1974 immigration freeze.
Les Trente Glorieuses
Post-war economic boom (1945-1975) drawing labour from abroad.
L'Armistice
Signed 22 June 1940, ending fighting and dividing France into occupied and free zones.
La Milice
Vichy paramilitary force created 1943, hunting Resistance members and Jews.
La Revolution nationale
Vichy's authoritarian programme: Travail, Famille, Patrie (Work, Family, Fatherland).
La zone libre
Southern unoccupied zone administered by Vichy until November 1942.
Le regime de Vichy
Collaborationist French government 1940-44, headquartered in Vichy.
Philippe Petain
WWI hero who became head of l'Etat francais and collaborated with Nazi Germany.
Charles de Gaulle
First president of the Fifth Republic (1959-1969), founder of the system.
Emmanuel Macron
President elected 2017, re-elected 2022, leader of Renaissance party.
Francois Mitterrand
First socialist president (1981-1995), led France for 14 years.
La Cinquieme Republique
Current French Republic, founded in 1958 under Charles de Gaulle.
Le quinquennat
Five-year presidential term, introduced in 2000 (previously seven-year septennat).
Semi-presidential system
France's hybrid model with a powerful directly-elected president and a prime minister.
